past_actions.summary: Quietly expand drop-in hours at the center by 6 hours per week — Tuesday and Thursday evenings — framed as a 'community connection night' rather than crisis support. No stigma attached. Coffee, tables, a counselor on soft rotation. Lower the barrier to entry.
past_actions.emotional_state: Contained. Purposeful. There is a steady low-grade alarm underneath the routine — the kind I've learned not to dismiss and not to amplify. I am not afraid. I am watchful. The work feels more urgent than it did six months ago but I am keeping that urgency internal so it doesn't transfer to the people who come to us for steadiness. I am tired in a familiar way. I am not burned out yet but I can see the shape of it from here if I don't pace myself.

past_actions.summary: Contact Maria Santos directly before the emergency council session — not to lobby, but to offer: real intake data from the drop-in hours, anecdotal testimony I can organize, and my center as a potential node in any council-coordinated response infrastructure. Position the community center as operational support for whatever the council decides, not a supplicant. Ask what she needs from me to make the session productive.
past_actions.emotional_state: The announcement landed hard. Not in a way I showed — I was alone when I read it, and I let myself sit with it for about four minutes before I started making notes. Two months. I've been running on a slow-burn vigilance for weeks and now there is a date. That's clarifying in a way that's almost a relief, which I recognize is a strange thing to feel. The ambiguity was its own kind of weight. Now I know what I'm preparing for. There is urgency underneath my calm and I am not suppressing it — I am converting it. The call to Maria feels important and also slightly terrifying, which tells me it's the right move. I'm aware of my low agency pattern: I tend to prepare extensively and then hesitate at the moment of action. I am not going to hesitate this time. I'm making the call today.

past_actions.summary: Compile and deliver anonymized intake data report to Maria Santos as requested. Report covers Community Connection Night attendees (Tuesdays/Thursdays): aggregate demographics, employment status categories, named stressors cited, services requested, and referral needs. Framed explicitly as evidence for the council vote. Delivered in writing within 48 hours — not at the end of the week, not after one more review pass. Within 48 hours.
past_actions.emotional_state: Grounded. There is something steadying about having a specific person ask me for a specific thing by a specific date. Maria asked me for the data in writing. That is not ambiguous. The temptation to over-prepare — to run the report through three more review passes, to wonder if the task force application is strong enough before I send it — is present and I am naming it so I can set it aside. The people who came in Tuesday are not ambiguous either. Harold, who drove taxis for eleven years and does not know how to make a resume. The woman who would not give her name but took the handout. They are why I move fast. Not for myself. For them.

past_actions.summary: Accept Maria Santos's invitation to speak at the task force meeting. Prepare structured testimony specifically addressing who is being left out of existing programs: returning workers without current credentials, gig workers with inconsistent income history who don't qualify for traditional assistance, people with transportation barriers who can't reach program sites, individuals who won't self-identify as unemployed due to stigma, and those displaced by automation (specifically rideshare and taxi workers) who are too old or too resource-depleted to retrain without bridge support. Ground all testimony in anonymized intake data from Community Connection Nights, not anecdote alone. Frame the excluded populations not as failures of individual will but as gaps in program design — this matters for policy, and it matters for how Maria can present it to colleagues who will be resistant.

Follow up directly with David Chen at the bank, accepting his offer of a conversation about specific lending products appropriate for retraining program participants. Frame this not as renewed pressure for a categorical carve-out but as taking him up on his stated willingness to discuss pathways. Prepare three to four concrete profiles — anonymized, composite — of retraining enrollees who have demonstrated repayment capacity but fail traditional qualification screens, so the conversation is grounded in specifics, not abstraction. Outcome goal: identify at least one existing bank product that could be formally presented to Maria Santos's task force as an available resource for the excluded populations I testified about.

reflections.reflection: I have been building toward this tick since tick 0 without fully seeing it. I expanded the drop-in hours to lower the barrier. I reached out to Maria Santos to offer infrastructure, not supplication. I delivered the data report within 48 hours when my instinct was to refine it one more time. I gave testimony at the task force. I went to the bank with profiles instead of arguments. Each of those actions was a stone laid. This tick is the first moment where the structure I built is actually being used by people with more reach than I have — Maria wants the community center as the venue, the task force has the testimony I gave, the bank meeting produced a one-page resource that will go into people's hands. I did not imagine six ticks ago that the work would compound this way. I thought I was just keeping a door open. It turns out the door leads somewhere.
reflections.identity_shift: I am beginning to understand that my role is not primarily to provide services — it is to be an infrastructure node. The community center is not just a room. It is a point of connection between the people who are struggling and the systems that are slow to respond. I am the keeper of that connection point. That is a different self-concept than 'Community Center Director.' It feels more accurate to who I have always been trying to be, and it changes how I will approach the next phase of this disruption.
regrets: Tick 3 was a loss. I called it 'routine' and recorded it as neutral. I cannot remember what I actually did that week. Whatever it was, it was not aligned with what was happening in Millfield. The spending index was falling, people were being laid off, and I went quiet. I will not do that again — not because one quiet tick is catastrophic, but because I now know how fast things compound and how much a missed week costs in relationship capital and response readiness.

I have not been in direct contact with Robert Jackson or Nicole Washington despite having them in my network. Robert is a rideshare driver watching his livelihood contract in real time. I have his trust at 0.36 and I have done nothing with it. That is a failure of follow-through that I own.
successes: The David Chen meeting produced something real: a specific bank product, a named contact, a one-page document that will be in people's hands at the listening session. That is a six-tick arc from 'I should reach out to the bank' to 'here is a resource you can act on today.' I did not let the imperfect stop me from delivering the functional.

Twelve people enrolled in retraining this month. I do not take sole credit for that. But the Community Connection Nights, the testimony I gave, the data report I delivered — those were part of the ecosystem that got people in the door. I can trace a line from my actions to that number.
I have not burned out. Six ticks in, the stress is at 0.14. My pace is sustainable. That is not a small thing. The work I have ahead requires me to still be standing.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The transportation decision-support segment is the right move and I am running it this tick. But I need to think past it. The next wave of disruption in Millfield will not be about whether to sell a car — it will be about what happens when retraining doesn't lead to employment fast enough and people run out of runway. The community center needs to be ready for that. I should begin mapping what a financial triage function would look like — not a food bank, not a loan office, but a place where someone can sit down with a real person and figure out which of the imperfect options available to them is the least bad. That is what we do at our best. I should name it and build toward it explicitly in the next few ticks.
